definitions.gloss: furigana, reading aid, phonetic gloss written above or beside kanji
definitions.explanation: Small kana characters placed above (in horizontal text) or beside (in vertical text) kanji to indicate their pronunciation. Used in children's books, language learning materials, and to clarify rare or unusual readings.

examples.japanese: {難|むずか}しい{漢字|かんじ}に{振|ふ}り{仮名|がな}をつける。
examples.english: To add furigana to difficult kanji.

examples.japanese: {子供向|こどもむ}けの{本|ほん}にはすべての{漢字|かんじ}に{振|ふ}り{仮名|がな}がついている。
examples.english: In books for children, all kanji have furigana.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}の{欄|らん}に{振|ふ}り{仮名|がな}も{記入|きにゅう}してください。
examples.english: Please also fill in the furigana in the name field.

notes:
{振|ふ}り{仮名|がな} is the standard term for the small phonetic readings placed alongside kanji. The word comes from {振|ふ}る (to assign, to allocate) + {仮名|かな} (kana characters).

Also written as ふりがな (all kana) in everyday usage.

TYPES:
- {総|そう}ルビ: full furigana on every kanji (common in children's materials)
- パラルビ: selective furigana only on difficult kanji

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {振|ふ}り{仮名|がな}をつける / {振|ふ}り{仮名|がな}を{振|ふ}る: to add furigana
- {振|ふ}り{仮名|がな}つき: with furigana included
- {振|ふ}り{仮名|がな}{欄|らん}: furigana field (on forms)

NOTE: On Japanese official forms, there is usually a space above or below the name field labeled ふりがな (written in hiragana, meaning write the reading in hiragana) or フリガナ (written in katakana, meaning write the reading in katakana).
